title: Temporal Uncertainty Calibration in Sequential Neural Networks
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods often assume static or batch-level uncertainty, neglecting the dynamic nature of sequential data where uncertainty evolves over time. We propose a temporal uncertainty calibration framework that jointly learns uncertainty distributions across time steps using recurrent architectures with adaptive uncertainty propagation, where each layer's uncertainty is updated via a time-aware calibration loss that accounts for temporal dependencies. This approach is evaluated on time-series forecasting tasks using both synthetic and real-world datasets, measuring calibration via time-dependent reliability diagrams and out-of-sample prediction entropy.

title: Dynamic Calibration via Adaptive Uncertainty Propagation
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods assume static uncertainty distributions over time, ignoring the dynamic nature of neural network predictions during inference. We propose a framework that adaptively propagates uncertainty through layers using real-time feedback from prediction confidence and error distributions, adjusting calibration parameters on-the-fly based on observed data stream characteristics. This dynamic calibration is evaluated using a multi-task, time-varying dataset where uncertainty drift is introduced, and performance is measured via both calibration error (e.g., Expected Calibration Error) and real-world decision accuracy under uncertainty.

title: Temporal Calibration in Sequential Neural Predictions
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods assume static or batch-wise uncertainty, ignoring the temporal evolution of confidence in sequential prediction tasks like time series forecasting. We propose a dynamic calibration framework that tracks and adjusts uncertainty estimates over time using a recurrent uncertainty model trained to learn temporal dependencies in prediction confidence, incorporating feedback from actual future outcomes. The framework is evaluated on real-world time series datasets by measuring temporal consistency of uncertainty estimates, using metrics such as temporal calibration error and surprise loss over prediction horizons.

title: Temporal Calibration Dynamics in Sequential Uncertainty Prediction
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods assume static or batch-wise uncertainty, but in sequential tasks (e.g., time-series forecasting or dialogue systems), uncertainty evolves over time. We propose a framework that models the temporal dynamics of calibration by tracking how uncertainty predictions evolve and adapt across time steps, using a recurrent calibration module that learns to correct for temporal biases in confidence estimation. This approach is evaluated by comparing its calibration performance—measured via the reliability diagram and expected calibration error—against baseline methods across diverse sequential datasets under varying time horizons and noise levels.

title: Dynamic Uncertainty Weighting for Ensemble Calibration
text: Current ensemble methods assume equal uncertainty contributions from each model, but in practice, individual models may have varying confidence in different domains or data distributions. We propose a dynamic uncertainty weighting mechanism that adaptively assigns weights to ensemble members based on real-time prediction variance and domain-specific performance metrics, allowing the system to prioritize reliable models during uncertain predictions. The approach is evaluated using a novel calibration metric that measures not only the confidence interval coverage but also the temporal stability of uncertainty propagation across sequential predictions in real-world applications.

title: Temporal Calibration Networks for Dynamic Uncertainty Evolution
text: Current uncertainty calibration methods assume static confidence distributions, ignoring that uncertainty in real-world tasks evolves over time due to changing data distributions or environmental shifts. We propose a temporal calibration network that learns to adapt uncertainty estimates dynamically by incorporating temporal dependencies in training data, using a recurrent uncertainty module that tracks confidence evolution across time steps. The method is evaluated on time-series forecasting and continual learning tasks by measuring the temporal alignment between predicted and true uncertainty, using metrics like temporal calibration loss and dynamic reliability diagrams.

title: Temporal Calibration in Sequential Decision-Making
text: Existing uncertainty calibration methods assume static or batch-level uncertainty, neglecting the dynamic nature of uncertainty evolution over time in sequential tasks. We propose a temporal calibration framework that models uncertainty propagation through time using a recurrent uncertainty network (RUN), where the network jointly learns both predictions and confidence estimates while adapting calibration dynamics across time steps. Evaluation is performed on sequential decision tasks like robotics control and dialogue systems using temporal calibration loss, temporal reliability scores, and future prediction accuracy under varying observation noise.

title: Temporal Calibration in Sequential Decision-Making

title: Fast and Accurate Quality Control of PET Bottle Caps Using Image Calibration and Lightweight CNNs
text: Current product quality control in food and pharmaceutical industries requires precise, contactless inspection using machine vision, but real-time performance is often limited by long inference or training times in deep learning models. This research proposes a novel data preprocessing method that leverages prior knowledge of the optical system to calibrate images, enabling a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to efficiently classify PET bottle cap defects. The approach is evaluated by comparing prediction and training times—showing at least five-fold improvements over standard models—while maintaining equivalent accuracy on ImageNet-trained benchmarks.

title: Incorporating input uncertainty in deep regression via Errors-in-Variables models
text: Deep neural networks often ignore uncertainty in input features, which can lead to biased or overly confident predictions. This research proposes using a Bayesian framework with Errors-in-Variables modeling to explicitly account for input uncertainty, thereby decomposing predictive uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. The approach is evaluated through simulated and real-world examples, comparing uncertainty coverage and prediction performance against standard deep regression models, with emphasis on improved reliability in known regression settings.

title: Post-stack seismic inversion using probabilistic and deep neural networks
text: Seismic inversion is a nonlinear, non-unique, and error-prone problem that traditionally relies on model-based methods, which can be unreliable. This research proposes using probabilistic neural networks (PNN) and deep feedforward neural networks (DFNN) to invert post-stack seismic data and extract porosity, gamma rays, and Lamé impedances, comparing results with model-based inversion (MBI). The performance of each method is evaluated by comparing predicted values with well-log data and through geological interpretation, such as time-slice analysis of deltaic environments, to assess geological correlation and reliability.

title: Generating backdoor samples for image caption models via trigger injection
text: Image caption models are vulnerable to backdoor attacks where adversarial triggers cause misclassification of target classes. We propose injecting a specific trigger into original images to create backdoor samples that the model misrecognizes as a target class during caption generation. The attack is evaluated using the MS-COCO dataset with Tensorflow, measuring the average attack success rate and comparing it to the original sample's error rate.

title: Robustness against adversarial attacks through diversity adversarial training
text: Deep neural networks, while effective in image and pattern recognition, are vulnerable to adversarial attacks where small noise perturbations cause misclassification. This research proposes a diversity adversarial training method that enhances model robustness by training the model on a variety of adversarial samples during training. The approach is evaluated by measuring the reduction in attack success rate and maintaining high accuracy on original data using MNIST and Fashion-MNIST datasets.

title: Automatic Modulation Classification with Deep Neural Networks
text: Many modern communication systems require accurate modulation classification to efficiently manage spectrum usage in crowded environments. This research proposes a comprehensive ablation study of convolutional neural network architectures to evaluate the impact of design elements such as dilated convolutions, statistics pooling, and squeeze-and-excitation units on classification accuracy. The approach evaluates performance on the RadioML 2018.01A dataset, focusing on peak accuracy (98.9%) and overall accuracy (63.7%), as well as performance across varying burst lengths, common misclassifications, and modulation categories.

title: Uncertainty-aware Race Recognition Using Fine-tuned VGG Networks
text: Current race recognition systems, such as the RR-VGG model, provide high accuracy but lack confidence estimation for individual predictions. By integrating uncertainty quantification—specifically, using methods from Paper 2 to estimate prediction confidence—into the RR-VGG framework, we can develop a system that not only identifies race but also assesses the reliability of each prediction. This uncertainty-aware system would be evaluated on the VNFaces dataset by measuring both classification accuracy and uncertainty estimation performance, such as mean average precision and confidence interval coverage, to determine if the model can effectively flag ambiguous or low-confidence cases for human review.
